claims.text: The dataset (SESAME) was generated for the Portuguese language.
The authors propose a method to automatically generate labeled datasets for NER from public data sources by exploiting links and structured data from DBpedia and Wikipedia.
They present a method to generate a massively-sized labeled dataset for NER in an automatic fashion, without human labor involved in labeling.
The authors propose a method to construct labeled datasets without human supervision for NER, using DBpedia and Wikipedia.
The work is described as constructing a massive, weakly-supervised dataset (a silver-standard corpus), not a gold-standard dataset.
A major difference from a similar approach is that they use an auxiliary NER predictor to capture missing entities, yielding denser annotations.
论文提出一种方法，利用DBpedia和Wikipedia中的链接与结构化数据，从公共数据源自动生成用于NER的标注数据集；由此得到的数据集SESAME由数百万条标注句子组成。
论文明确表示，其提出的方法是在没有人工监督的情况下为NER构建标注数据集，使用的是按语义网原则组织起来的公共数据源DBpedia和Wikipedia。
作者在结论中说明，该方法是自动生成大规模标注NER数据集，标注过程中没有人工参与，依靠Wikipedia和DBpedia的结构化数据来检测文章中的命名实体提及。
SESAME是使用该提出方法生成的葡萄牙语NER大规模数据集，其全称为Silver-Standard Named Entity Recognition dataset。
该工作被描述为构建一个大规模弱监督数据集（即银标准语料库），并使用辅助NER预测器捕获缺失实体，从而得到更密集的标注。
SESAME不是金标准数据集，但允许以弱监督方式训练数据需求大的预测器，从而缓解对人工标注数据的需求。
论文称其数据集是通过自动生成的方法产生的，方法细节在正文相应章节给出。
实验显示，单独使用SESAME不如使用人工标注的HAREM2语料训练的网络；但SESAME与HAREM2一起使用时，F1分数提升1.5。

The SESAME paper (Building a Massive Corpus for NER) proposes a method to automatically generate labeled datasets for NER from public data sources (DBpedia and Wikipedia); the resulting SESAME dataset is described as a massive, weakly-supervised silver-standard corpus constructed without human supervision, with its methodology stated to automatically generate the dataset.

The Croatian MT paper (A Lost Croatian Cybernetic Machine Translation Program) describes historical research on machine translation by Bulcsu Laszlo's group in Yugoslavia in the 1950s and early 1960s; the supplied evidence does not describe any dataset generation for that paper, so the question of a completely automatically generated dataset does not apply in the same sense.
The Croatian paper explicitly connects its subject to the beginnings of machine translation in the USA and USSR, motivated by the Cold War and intelligence needs of the period.

The Croatian paper surveys four major USSR machine translation approaches in the late 1950s, noting that the information-theoretic (cybernetic) approach of Lyapunov, Kulagina and Dobrushin was the main role model for the Croatian efforts from 1957 onwards.
The Croatian paper presents the Croatian group's approach as different from the usual logical approaches of the period, advocating cybernetic methods later adopted as canon by mainstream AI.

The SESAME paper does not, in the supplied evidence, make any comparison to US or USSR research; it instead positions itself relative to prior automatic Wikipedia-based dataset creation work and distant learning approaches.

The two papers are not directly comparable on these questions: one is a historical study of 1950s-60s Croatian machine translation in the context of US/USSR work, and the other is a modern NLP methodology paper on automatically building a weakly-supervised NER corpus; the US/USSR comparison question is only addressed by the Croatian paper.
